# Appendix A. Single-modality derivations {#sec-appendix-a .unnumbered}

<!-- REVISIT R1 START -->
<!-- REVISIT R2 START -->

This appendix starts from the likelihood, priors and variational family of the single-modality model and derives, for each coordinate, the pseudo-observation $x = B/A$ and standard error $s = A^{-1/2}$ passed to the empirical-Bayes normal-means (EBNM) solver. It then states where the evaluated algorithm departs from the joint target. Throughout, $\bar\theta = E_q\theta$ and $\overline{\theta^2} = E_q\theta^2$ for the variational posterior $q$, and $E_{-\theta}$ denotes expectation under $q$ over every coordinate except $\theta$.

<!-- REVISIT R2 END -->
<!-- REVISIT R1 END -->

## A.1 Model, target and evaluated algorithm {.unnumbered}

<!-- REVISIT R1 START -->
<!-- REVISIT R2 START -->

**Reconstruction likelihood.** With $e_{ij} \sim N(0, \tau_j^{-1})$ in @eq-recon,
$$
\ell_Y = \sum_{i,j}\Big\{\tfrac12\log\frac{\tau_j}{2\pi} - \frac{\tau_j}{2}\Big(y_{ij} - \sum_k L_{ik}F_{jk}\Big)^2\Big\}.
$$ {#eq-a-lY}

**Cox partial likelihood.** Let $s_1 < s_2 < \cdots$ be the distinct death times, $\mathcal D_a$ the patients who die at $s_a$, $d_a = |\mathcal D_a|$, and $\mathcal R_a = \{i : t_i \ge s_a\}$ the risk set. With Breslow's handling of ties,
$$
\ell_C(\eta) = \sum_a\Big\{\sum_{i\in\mathcal D_a}\eta_i - d_a\log\sum_{i\in\mathcal R_a}e^{\eta_i}\Big\}.
$$ {#eq-a-lC}
The partial likelihood is not a full likelihood for the survival times; using it as the survival term defines a partial-likelihood joint target rather than a fully specified generative model.

**Priors.** $L_{ik} \sim g_{L,k}$ and $F_{jk} \sim g_{F,k}$, each a point mass at zero mixed with an exponential distribution, and $\tilde\beta_k \sim g_{\beta,k} = N(0, \sigma_k^2)$, all independent. The residual precisions $\tau_j$ and the prior parameters are point estimates.

**Joint target.** In the target, the predictor uses the random loadings, $\eta_i = \sum_k\tilde\beta_k\,y_i^\top u_k(F)$, where the normalized direction is $u_k(F) = F_{\cdot k}/d_k(F)$ with $d_k(F) = \lVert F_{\cdot k}\rVert_2$ when $d_k(F) > 0$, and $u_k(F) = 0$ when the column is identically zero, an event with positive probability under the point-mass prior. This convention defines the target; it does not change the evaluated fits, whose stored norms include a small ridge (A.10). The Gaussian coordinate updates below additionally hold $d_k$ fixed. With the mean-field family
$$
q(L, F, \tilde\beta) = \prod_{i,k} q(L_{ik})\prod_{j,k} q(F_{jk})\prod_k q(\tilde\beta_k),
$$
the variational objective is
$$
\mathcal L(q) = E_q\ell_Y + E_q\ell_C(\eta) - \sum_{i,k}\mathrm{KL}\big(q(L_{ik})\,\Vert\, g_{L,k}\big) - \sum_{j,k}\mathrm{KL}\big(q(F_{jk})\,\Vert\, g_{F,k}\big) - \sum_k\mathrm{KL}\big(q(\tilde\beta_k)\,\Vert\, g_{\beta,k}\big).
$$ {#eq-a-target}

**Evaluated algorithm.** Two features make the evaluated algorithm differ from coordinate ascent on @eq-a-target. First, at the start of sweep $r$ it fixes $D^{(r)} = \mathrm{diag}(\lVert\bar F^{(r-1)}_{\cdot k}\rVert_2)$ and the projection $\tilde Z^{(r)} = Y\bar F^{(r-1)}[D^{(r)}]^{-1}$ and treats $\tilde Z$ as a known covariate matrix for the rest of the sweep, so the coefficient update has no projection variance. Second, $E_q\ell_C$ is replaced by the expectation of the working quadratic of A.2. $L$ does not enter $\eta$ in either the target or the algorithm.

<!-- REVISIT R2 END -->
<!-- REVISIT R1 END -->

## A.2 Cox working approximation {#sec-appendix-a-cox .unnumbered}

<!-- REVISIT R1 START -->

Let $\hat\eta$ be the predictor at the start of a sweep and
$$
P_{ai} = \frac{\mathbf 1\{i\in\mathcal R_a\}\,e^{\hat\eta_i}}{\sum_{l\in\mathcal R_a}e^{\hat\eta_l}},
$$
the share of risk-set member $i$ at death time $s_a$.

**Score.** Differentiating @eq-a-lC, $\partial\big(d_a\log\sum_{l\in\mathcal R_a}e^{\eta_l}\big)/\partial\eta_i = d_aP_{ai}$, so
$$
u_i = \frac{\partial\ell_C}{\partial\eta_i}\Big|_{\hat\eta} = \delta_i - \sum_a d_aP_{ai}.
$$
The Breslow cumulative baseline hazard is $\hat H_0(t) = \sum_{a: s_a\le t}d_a/\sum_{l\in\mathcal R_a}e^{\hat\eta_l}$. Because $i \in \mathcal R_a$ exactly when $s_a \le t_i$,
$$
a_i \equiv e^{\hat\eta_i}\hat H_0(t_i) = \sum_a d_aP_{ai}, \qquad u_i = \delta_i - a_i .
$$

**Exact curvature.** Differentiating again, $\partial^2\big(d_a\log\sum_{l\in\mathcal R_a}e^{\eta_l}\big)/\partial\eta_i\partial\eta_h = d_a(P_{ai}\mathbf 1\{i = h\} - P_{ai}P_{ah})$, so the negative Hessian is
$$
\mathcal H = \sum_a d_a\big\{\mathrm{diag}(P_a) - P_aP_a^\top\big\}, \qquad \mathcal H_{ii} = \sum_a d_aP_{ai}(1 - P_{ai}) = a_i - \sum_a d_aP_{ai}^2 .
$$
$\mathcal H$ couples patients through shared risk sets, and its diagonal is smaller than $a_i$.

**Working replacement.** The algorithm keeps the exact score and replaces $\mathcal H$ by $W = \mathrm{diag}(w)$ with $w_i = \max(a_i, 10^{-6})$, a Poisson-style working curvature. The resulting surrogate is
$$
\ell_C(\eta) \approx \ell_C(\hat\eta) + \sum_i u_i(\eta_i - \hat\eta_i) - \tfrac12\sum_i w_i(\eta_i - \hat\eta_i)^2 .
$$
Expanding $(\eta_i - \hat\eta_i)^2 = \eta_i^2 - 2\eta_i\hat\eta_i + \hat\eta_i^2$ and collecting terms that do not involve $\eta$ into a constant $c$,
$$
\ell_C(\eta) \approx c + \sum_i\Big\{(u_i + w_i\hat\eta_i)\eta_i - \tfrac12 w_i\eta_i^2\Big\}.
$$ {#eq-a-linear}
For $w_i > 0$, completing the square with $z_i = \hat\eta_i + u_i/w_i$ gives $(u_i + w_i\hat\eta_i)\eta_i - \frac12w_i\eta_i^2 = w_iz_i\eta_i - \frac12w_i\eta_i^2 = -\frac12w_i(z_i - \eta_i)^2 + \frac12w_iz_i^2$, so
$$
\ell_C(\eta) \approx c' - \tfrac12\sum_i w_i(z_i - \eta_i)^2 .
$$ {#eq-a-working}
At the floor, $w_i = 10^{-6}$ while $u_i = \delta_i - a_i$ is retained. When risk sets are stratified, $P_{ai}$ and $\hat H_0$ are formed within strata; the evaluated fit has no strata. The surrogate is a working approximation, not the second-order Taylor expansion of $\ell_C$.

<!-- REVISIT R1 END -->

## A.3 Reduction to empirical-Bayes normal means {.unnumbered}

For one scalar coordinate $\theta$ with prior $g$, the optimal mean-field factor satisfies
$$
\log q^*(\theta) = E_{-\theta}\big[\text{log likelihood terms}\big] + \log g(\theta) + c .
$$
In every update below, the expected likelihood terms are quadratic in $\theta$, $B\theta - \frac12A\theta^2 + c$ with $A > 0$. Completing the square,
$$
B\theta - \tfrac12A\theta^2 = -\tfrac12A\Big(\theta - \frac BA\Big)^2 + \frac{B^2}{2A},
$$
so
$$
q^*(\theta) \propto N(x;\, \theta, s^2)\,g(\theta), \qquad x = B/A, \quad s = A^{-1/2}.
$$ {#eq-a-ebnm}
This is the posterior of $\theta$ given one Gaussian observation $x$ with standard error $s$. When $H$ coordinates $\theta_1, \dots, \theta_H$ share a prior, the prior is estimated by maximizing the marginal likelihood of their pseudo-observations,
$$
\hat g = \arg\max_g\sum_{h=1}^H\log p_g(x_h), \qquad p_g(x_h) = \int N(x_h;\, \theta, s_h^2)\,g(d\theta),
$$
and each $q(\theta_h)$ is the posterior under $\hat g$.

**KL identity.** For the posterior under the same prior, $q(\theta) = N(x; \theta, s^2)g(\theta)/p_g(x)$, so $\log q(\theta) - \log g(\theta) = \log N(x; \theta, s^2) - \log p_g(x)$ and
$$
\mathrm{KL}(q\,\Vert\,g) = E_q\log N(x;\, \theta, s^2) - \log p_g(x).
$$ {#eq-a-kl}
For a vector of $H$ coordinates with a common precision $A$,
$$
\sum_h E_q\log N(x_h;\, \theta_h, A^{-1}) = \frac H2\log\frac{A}{2\pi} - \frac A2\sum_h\big(x_h^2 - 2x_h\bar\theta_h + \overline{\theta_h^2}\big).
$$ {#eq-a-kl-vector}
If $A = B = 0$ the coordinate receives no information and the update is prior-only, $q = g$; the normal-means inputs $x = B/A$ and $s = A^{-1/2}$ require $A > 0$.

<!-- REVISIT R1 START -->

The single-modality implementation floors each $A$ at $10^{-10}$, which gives a very large $s$ and a posterior indistinguishable from the prior. The multimodal implementation handles the boundary separately (B.5).

<!-- REVISIT R1 END -->

## A.4 Posteriors under point-mass priors {.unnumbered}

<!-- REVISIT R1 START -->

**Point-exponential prior.** Let $g = (1-\pi)\delta_0 + \pi\,\lambda e^{-\lambda\theta}\mathbf 1\{\theta > 0\}$. For the slab, expand the exponent and complete the square with $m = x - \lambda s^2$:
$$
-\frac{(\theta - x)^2}{2s^2} - \lambda\theta = -\frac{(\theta - m)^2}{2s^2} - \lambda x + \frac{\lambda^2 s^2}{2},
$$
which follows from $m^2 - x^2 = -2\lambda s^2x + \lambda^2s^4$. Hence $N(x; \theta, s^2)\lambda e^{-\lambda\theta} = \lambda\exp(-\lambda x + \lambda^2s^2/2)\,N(\theta; m, s^2)$, and integrating over $\theta > 0$ gives $\lambda\exp(-\lambda x + \lambda^2s^2/2)\,\Phi(m/s)$. The marginal likelihood and posterior weights are therefore
$$
p_g(x) = (1-\pi)N(x;\, 0, s^2) + \pi\lambda e^{-\lambda x + \lambda^2s^2/2}\,\Phi(m/s), \qquad
\omega_0 = \frac{(1-\pi)N(x; 0, s^2)}{p_g(x)}, \quad \omega_+ = 1 - \omega_0,
$$
and the posterior is $\omega_0\delta_0$ plus $\omega_+$ times $N(m, s^2)$ truncated to $(0, \infty)$.

**Truncated-normal moments.** Write $\theta = m + s\zeta$ with $\zeta$ standard normal conditioned on $\zeta > -a$, $a = m/s$, and let $r = \phi(a)/\Phi(a)$. Using $\int_{-a}^\infty \zeta\phi(\zeta)\,d\zeta = \phi(a)$ and, by parts, $\int_{-a}^\infty\zeta^2\phi(\zeta)\,d\zeta = \Phi(a) - a\phi(a)$, we have $E\zeta = r$ and $E\zeta^2 = 1 - ar$. Hence
$$
M_+(m) = E\theta = m + sr, \qquad S_+(m) = E\theta^2 = m^2 + 2msr + s^2(1 - ar) = m^2 + s^2 + msr,
$$ {#eq-a-trunc}
and the posterior moments are $\bar\theta = \omega_+M_+(m)$ and $\overline{\theta^2} = \omega_+S_+(m)$. For large negative $a$, $\log\Phi(a)$ and $r$ are evaluated with tail approximations for numerical stability. The point-Laplace case used in the multimodal model is derived in Appendix B.6.

<!-- REVISIT R1 END -->

## A.5 Coefficient update {.unnumbered}

<!-- REVISIT R1 START -->
<!-- REVISIT R2 START -->

Fix $k$ and write $a_i = \tilde Z_{ik}$, which is a known covariate within the sweep, and $H_i = \sum_{l\ne k}\tilde Z_{il}\tilde\beta_l$, which does not involve $\tilde\beta_k$. Then $\eta_i = H_i + a_i\tilde\beta_k$. The survival weight $\alpha$ multiplies the working term @eq-a-working, so the terms involving $\tilde\beta_k$ are $-\frac{\alpha}{2}\sum_iw_i(z_i - H_i - a_i\tilde\beta_k)^2$. Expanding the square,
$$
(z_i - H_i - a_i\tilde\beta_k)^2 = (z_i - H_i)^2 - 2a_i\tilde\beta_k(z_i - H_i) + a_i^2\tilde\beta_k^2,
$$
and taking $E_{-\tilde\beta_k}$, under which $E(z_i - H_i) = z_i - \bar H_i$ and $E(z_i - H_i)^2$ is a constant $c_i$,
$$
E_{-\tilde\beta_k}(z_i - H_i - a_i\tilde\beta_k)^2 = c_i - 2a_i\tilde\beta_k(z_i - \bar H_i) + a_i^2\tilde\beta_k^2 .
$$
Multiplying by $-\alpha w_i/2$ and summing over $i$,
$$
\tilde\beta_k\,\alpha\sum_iw_ia_i(z_i - \bar H_i) - \tfrac12\tilde\beta_k^2\,\alpha\sum_iw_ia_i^2 + c,
$$
so
$$
A_{\beta,k} = \alpha\sum_iw_i\tilde Z_{ik}^2, \qquad B_{\beta,k} = \alpha\sum_iw_i\tilde Z_{ik}(z_i - \bar H_i), \qquad x_{\beta,k} = \frac{\sum_iw_i\tilde Z_{ik}(z_i - \bar H_i)}{\sum_iw_i\tilde Z_{ik}^2}, \qquad s_{\beta,k} = A_{\beta,k}^{-1/2}.
$$ {#eq-a-beta}
For $\alpha > 0$ the pseudo-observation does not depend on $\alpha$, and the standard error is inflated by $\alpha^{-1/2}$ ($\sqrt 2$ at $\alpha = 0.5$), provided the floor on $A$ is inactive. Under the working-quadratic approximation with random loadings, the quadratic coefficient would involve $E(\tilde Z_{ik}^2)$; the evaluated plug-in update instead uses $\tilde Z_{ik}^2$ and does not pass loading uncertainty to the coefficient. Under the exact target, $E_q\ell_C$ is not quadratic in $\tilde\beta_k$ and has no conjugate update.

**Normal prior.** Let $g_{\beta,k} = N(0, v)$ with $v > 0$, and write $b$ for $\tilde\beta_k$. Expanding both squares and completing the square in $b$,
$$
\frac{(x - b)^2}{s^2} + \frac{b^2}{v} = \frac{(b - m)^2}{V} + \frac{x^2}{s^2 + v}, \qquad V = \frac{s^2v}{s^2 + v}, \quad m = \frac{xv}{s^2 + v},
$$
which follows because the coefficient of $b^2$ is $1/s^2 + 1/v = 1/V$, the coefficient of $b$ is $-2x/s^2 = -2m/V$, and the remaining constant is $x^2/s^2 - m^2/V = x^2/(s^2 + v)$. Restoring the normalizing constants, $(2\pi s^2)^{-1/2}(2\pi v)^{-1/2} = \{2\pi(s^2 + v)\}^{-1/2}(2\pi V)^{-1/2}$, so
$$
N(x;\, b, s^2)\,N(b;\, 0, v) = N(x;\, 0, s^2 + v)\,N(b;\, m, V).
$$
Integrating over $b$ gives the marginal $x \sim N(0, s^2 + v)$, and the remaining factor is the posterior $N(m, V)$. Writing $\sigma^2$ for $v$, the marginal log-likelihood is
$$
\ell(\sigma^2) = -\tfrac12\log\{2\pi(s^2 + \sigma^2)\} - \frac{x^2}{2(s^2 + \sigma^2)}, \qquad
\ell'(\sigma^2) = \frac{x^2 - (s^2 + \sigma^2)}{2(s^2 + \sigma^2)^2}.
$$
The derivative is positive for $\sigma^2 < x^2 - s^2$ and negative beyond, so the maximizer over $\sigma^2 \ge 0$ is
$$
\hat\sigma_k^2 = \max(0,\, x^2 - s^2).
$$
For $\hat\sigma_k^2 > 0$, the factorization above with $v = \hat\sigma_k^2$ gives
$$
\bar{\tilde\beta}_k = \frac{x\,\hat\sigma^2}{\hat\sigma^2 + s^2}, \qquad \mathrm{Var}(\tilde\beta_k) = \frac{\hat\sigma^2s^2}{\hat\sigma^2 + s^2}.
$$
If $|x| \le s$, then $\hat\sigma_k^2 = 0$ and $q(\tilde\beta_k)$ is the point mass at zero.

<!-- REVISIT R2 END -->
<!-- REVISIT R1 END -->

## A.6 Activity update {.unnumbered}

<!-- REVISIT R1 START -->

$L$ appears only in $\ell_Y$. Define the random residual excluding factor $k$, $r_{ij}^{(-k)} = y_{ij} - \sum_{l\ne k}L_{il}F_{jl}$, and its mean $R_{ij}^{(-k)} = E_q r_{ij}^{(-k)} = y_{ij} - \sum_{l\ne k}\bar L_{il}\bar F_{jl}$, which uses the independence of $L_{il}$ and $F_{jl}$ under $q$. The terms of @eq-a-lY involving $L_{ik}$ are $-\frac{\tau_j}{2}(r_{ij}^{(-k)} - L_{ik}F_{jk})^2$. Expanding,
$$
(r_{ij}^{(-k)} - L_{ik}F_{jk})^2 = (r_{ij}^{(-k)})^2 - 2L_{ik}r_{ij}^{(-k)}F_{jk} + L_{ik}^2F_{jk}^2 .
$$
Under $q$, $F_{jk}$ is independent of $r_{ij}^{(-k)}$, which involves only the other factors, so
$$
E_{-L_{ik}}(r_{ij}^{(-k)} - L_{ik}F_{jk})^2 = c_{ij} - 2L_{ik}R_{ij}^{(-k)}\bar F_{jk} + L_{ik}^2\overline{F_{jk}^2}.
$$
Multiplying by $-\tau_j/2$ and summing over $j$,
$$
A_{L,k} = \sum_j\tau_j\overline{F_{jk}^2}, \qquad B_{L,ik} = \sum_j\tau_jR_{ij}^{(-k)}\bar F_{jk}, \qquad x_{L,ik} = B_{L,ik}/A_{L,k}, \qquad s_{L,k} = A_{L,k}^{-1/2}.
$$ {#eq-a-L}
All $n$ pseudo-observations of factor $k$ share the precision $A_{L,k}$. The point-exponential prior $g_{L,k}$ is fitted by maximizing their joint marginal likelihood (A.3), and the posterior moments follow from A.4. Because $\eta$ does not depend on $L$, this update holds in every configuration of the model.

<!-- REVISIT R1 END -->

## A.7 Loading update {.unnumbered}

<!-- REVISIT R1 START -->

**Reconstruction terms.** Exchanging the roles of $L$ and $F$ in A.6, the terms of @eq-a-lY involving $F_{jk}$ are $-\frac{\tau_j}{2}\sum_i(r_{ij}^{(-k)} - L_{ik}F_{jk})^2$, and
$$
E_{-F_{jk}}(r_{ij}^{(-k)} - L_{ik}F_{jk})^2 = c_{ij} - 2F_{jk}R_{ij}^{(-k)}\bar L_{ik} + F_{jk}^2\overline{L_{ik}^2}.
$$
Multiplying by $-\tau_j/2$ and summing over $i$,
$$
A^{\mathrm{rec}}_{F,jk} = \tau_j\sum_i\overline{L_{ik}^2}, \qquad B^{\mathrm{rec}}_{F,jk} = \tau_j\sum_iR_{ij}^{(-k)}\bar L_{ik}.
$$ {#eq-a-F-gen}

**Survival terms of the target, with a fixed normalizer.** If $d_k$ depends on $F$, $\eta_i$ is not linear in $F_{jk}$ and the working term is not quadratic in it. Holding $d_k$ fixed, set $a_{ij} = y_{ij}/d_k$, $C_i = \sum_{h\ne j}a_{ih}F_{hk}$ and $H_i = \eta_{i,-k}$, so that $\eta_i = H_i + \tilde\beta_k(C_i + a_{ij}F_{jk})$. With $G_i = z_i - H_i - \tilde\beta_kC_i$,
$$
(z_i - \eta_i)^2 = G_i^2 - 2a_{ij}F_{jk}\tilde\beta_kG_i + a_{ij}^2\tilde\beta_k^2F_{jk}^2 .
$$
Under $q$, $\tilde\beta_k$, $H_i$ and $C_i$ are independent of each other and of $F_{jk}$, so $E(\tilde\beta_kG_i) = \bar{\tilde\beta}_k(z_i - \bar H_i) - \overline{\tilde\beta_k^2}\,\bar C_i$. Multiplying the expectation by $-w_i/2$ and summing over $i$ gives the coefficients
$$
A^{\mathrm{surv}}_{F,jk} = \overline{\tilde\beta_k^2}\sum_iw_i\frac{y_{ij}^2}{d_k^2}, \qquad
B^{\mathrm{surv}}_{F,jk} = \bar{\tilde\beta}_k\sum_iw_i\frac{y_{ij}}{d_k}(z_i - \bar H_i) - \overline{\tilde\beta_k^2}\sum_iw_i\frac{y_{ij}}{d_k}\bar C_i .
$$ {#eq-a-F-surv}
The last term couples feature $j$ to the other features of factor $k$ through $\bar C_i$.

**Implemented update.** The implementation combines the reconstruction terms with a simpler survival branch, using weights $1 - \alpha_F$ and $\alpha_F$:
$$
A_{F,jk} = (1-\alpha_F)A^{\mathrm{rec}}_{F,jk} + \alpha_F\overline{\tilde\beta_k^2}\sum_iw_iy_{ij}^2, \qquad
B_{F,jk} = (1-\alpha_F)B^{\mathrm{rec}}_{F,jk} + \alpha_F\bar{\tilde\beta}_k\sum_iw_iy_{ij}(z_i - \bar\eta_{i,-k}),
$$ {#eq-a-F}
with $x_{F,jk} = B_{F,jk}/A_{F,jk}$ and $s_{F,jk} = A_{F,jk}^{-1/2}$. Compared with @eq-a-F-surv, this branch omits the normalizer $d_k$ and the coupling term, and it updates all features of factor $k$ simultaneously. With $\alpha_F = 0.5$ the pseudo-observation equals that of the unit-weight sum of the reconstruction terms and this branch, with half its precision; this is a statement about the same approximate kernel, not an exact posterior of the normalized joint target. **In the evaluated fit $\alpha_F = 0$**, so @eq-a-F reduces to @eq-a-F-gen: the loading update is the reconstruction update of empirical-Bayes matrix factorization, with the point-exponential prior fitted over the $p$ pseudo-observations of each factor.

<!-- REVISIT R1 END -->

## A.8 Precision update {.unnumbered}

<!-- REVISIT R1 START -->

Write $\mu_{ij} = \sum_kL_{ik}F_{jk}$. Under $q$ the factors are independent, so $E\mu_{ij} = \sum_k\bar L_{ik}\bar F_{jk}$ and
$$
E\mu_{ij}^2 = \Big(\sum_k\bar L_{ik}\bar F_{jk}\Big)^2 + \sum_k\big(\overline{L_{ik}^2}\,\overline{F_{jk}^2} - \bar L_{ik}^2\bar F_{jk}^2\big),
$$
because $\mathrm{Var}(\mu_{ij}) = \sum_k\mathrm{Var}(L_{ik}F_{jk})$ and $\mathrm{Var}(L_{ik}F_{jk}) = \overline{L_{ik}^2}\,\overline{F_{jk}^2} - \bar L_{ik}^2\bar F_{jk}^2$. Hence
$$
Q_j = \sum_iE_q(y_{ij} - \mu_{ij})^2 = \sum_i\Big[(y_{ij} - E\mu_{ij})^2 + \sum_k\big(\overline{L_{ik}^2}\,\overline{F_{jk}^2} - \bar L_{ik}^2\bar F_{jk}^2\big)\Big].
$$
The expected log-likelihood in $\tau_j$ is $\frac n2\log\tau_j - \frac{\tau_j}{2}Q_j + c$; setting its derivative $n/(2\tau_j) - Q_j/2$ to zero gives
$$
\hat\tau_j = n/Q_j .
$$ {#eq-a-tau}
The implementation floors $Q_j$ at $n \times 10^{-8}$, so $\hat\tau_j \le 10^8$. There is no prior on $\tau_j$.

<!-- REVISIT R1 END -->

## A.9 Monitoring statistic and stopping rule {#sec-appendix-a-objective .unnumbered}

<!-- REVISIT R1 START -->

After each sweep the implementation computes
$$
J = (1-\alpha)\,G + \alpha\,p\,S + \sum_k\big(\kappa_{L,k} + \kappa_{F,k} + \kappa_{\beta,k}\big),
$$ {#eq-a-J}
where $G = \sum_j\big[\frac n2\log\tau_j - \frac{\tau_j}{2}Q_j\big]$ is the reconstruction log-likelihood without its constant, $S = \ell_C(\hat\eta) - \frac12\sum_iw_i\mathrm{Var}_q(\eta_i)$ with $\mathrm{Var}_q(\eta_i) = \sum_k\tilde Z_{ik}^2\mathrm{Var}_q(\tilde\beta_k)$ evaluated at the sweep's starting predictor $\hat\eta$, and each $\kappa$ is a negative KL term computed from @eq-a-kl. The algorithm stops at the first sweep after the fifth with $|J_r - J_{r-1}|/|J_{r-1}| < 10^{-5}$.

$J$ differs from the target @eq-a-target in four ways. Its reconstruction and survival components are weighted by $1-\alpha$ and $\alpha p$. Its survival term uses $\ell_C(\hat\eta)$ at the start of the sweep, whereas the expected working quadratic at the updated means would also include $\sum_iu_i(\bar\eta_i - \hat\eta_i) - \frac12\sum_iw_i(\bar\eta_i - \hat\eta_i)^2$. Its survival term uses the working curvature of A.2. And for the activities, whose $n$ pseudo-observations share one precision $A_{L,k}$, the implemented $\kappa_{L,k}$ includes the Gaussian log-normalizer $\frac12\log(A_{L,k}/2\pi)$ once rather than $n$ times as in @eq-a-kl-vector, so
$$
\kappa_{L,k}^{\mathrm{impl}} = \kappa_{L,k} + \frac{n-1}{2}\log\frac{A_{L,k}}{2\pi},
$$
a discrepancy that changes with $A_{L,k}$ across sweeps. These features affect only the stopping rule, not the coordinate updates. $J$ is therefore a convergence monitor, not an evidence lower bound, and the updates are not guaranteed to increase it.

<!-- REVISIT R1 END -->

## A.10 Orientation and prediction {.unnumbered}

<!-- REVISIT R2 START -->

For the evaluated single-modality fit, higher $\eta$ denotes longer survival. All external evaluations therefore use $\mathrm{risk} = -\eta$, a direction fixed from training. The stored second moments of $\tilde\beta$ equal the squared means, so this fit has no recoverable coefficient variance.

For a new patient with data standardized within its own cohort, prediction restricts $\bar F$ to the training features $\mathcal G$ measured in that cohort and keeps the stored norms $D_*$, formed from $\bar F$ at the start of the final sweep:
$$
\eta_{\mathrm{new}} = y_{\mathrm{new},\mathcal G}^\top\bar F_{\mathcal G}D_*^{-1}\bar{\tilde\beta}.
$$
$D_*$ differs slightly from the norms of the final $\bar F$ (by less than $2\times10^{-3}$ in absolute value for each retained program in the evaluated fit), and the stored norms include a ridge, $d_k = (\lVert\bar F_{\cdot k}\rVert_2^2 + 10^{-10})^{1/2}$, so a zero column gives a zero projection.

<!-- REVISIT R2 END -->


## A.11 Joint target and evaluated algorithm {.unnumbered}

<!-- REVISIT R1 START -->
<!-- REVISIT R2 START -->

| Component | Joint target @eq-a-target | Evaluated algorithm |
|------------|----------------------|----------------------|
| Survival term | $E_q\ell_C(\eta)$, exact partial likelihood | Expected working quadratic @eq-a-working with diagonal Poisson-style curvature, at the sweep's starting predictor |
| Predictor | $\eta$ uses random $F$ and the direction $u_k(F)$ | Projection $\tilde Z = Y\bar F D^{-1}$ from posterior means, fixed within a sweep; prediction uses stored $D_*$ |
| Coefficient update | Nonconjugate under the exact target; the random-projection working quadratic uses $E(\tilde Z_{ik}^2)$ | Plug-in working quadratic with $\tilde Z_{ik}^2$; working term weighted by $\alpha = 0.5$ |
| Activity update | Reconstruction only | Reconstruction only |
| Loading update | Reconstruction plus coupled survival term, requiring a fixed or differentiated $d_k$ | Reconstruction only ($\alpha_F = 0$) |
| Precision | Maximum likelihood | Maximum likelihood with a floor |
| Objective | $\mathcal L(q)$ | Monitoring statistic @eq-a-J, used only for stopping |
| Coefficient uncertainty | Posterior variance of $\tilde\beta$ | Stored variances are zero for the evaluated fit |

: Joint target and evaluated single-modality algorithm. Coordinate updates for $L$, $F$ and $\tau$ are exact for the reconstruction terms, so with $\alpha_F = 0$ they are the coordinate updates of empirical-Bayes matrix factorization, interleaved with an empirical-Bayes update of the Cox coefficients on fixed projections. $\mathcal L(q)$, variational objective; KL, Kullback–Leibler divergence; $\alpha$, $\alpha_F$, survival weights in the coefficient and loading updates; $D_*$, stored loading-column norms. {#tbl-math-vs-impl}
